verses.restored: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

familiar.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

notes.title: David, Bathsheba, and Uriah
notes.body: The superscription links this psalm to David after Nathan confronted him concerning Bathsheba. Any penitential reading must keep Bathsheba’s violated agency and Uriah’s killing visible rather than reducing the story to David’s private spiritual crisis.

modern.text: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.

original.text: בְּֽבוֹא אֵ֭לָיו נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כַּֽאֲשֶׁר בָּ֝֗א אֶל בַּת שָֽׁבַע חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי

familiar.text: Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

modern.text: Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.

original.text: כִּֽי פְ֭שָׁעַי אֲנִ֣י אֵדָ֑ע וְחַטָּאתִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד

verses.restored: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.

familiar.text: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.

notes.title: “Against you only”
notes.body: “Against you, you only, have I sinned” is confessional rhetoric before God; it cannot erase the concrete human beings harmed in the narrative associated with the psalm, especially Bathsheba and Uriah.

modern.text: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.

original.text: לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨ חָטָאתִי֮ וְהָרַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ עָ֫שִׂ֥יתִי לְ֭מַעַן תִּצְדַּ֥ק בְּדָבְרֶ֗ךָ תִּזְכֶּ֥ה בְשָׁפְטֶֽךָ

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Repentance must name harm to people, not erase victims behind private God-talk. The psalm must not excuse sexual abuse, murder, or leader immunity.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
